module


public import Mathlib.Topology.Separation.GDelta

@[expose] public section

/--
A space where all singletons are Gδ sets.
-/
class HasGδSingletons (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  isGδ_singleton : ∀ ⦃x : X⦄, IsGδ {x}

/-- Singletons are Gδ in first-countable T₁ spaces. -/
instance HasGδSingletons.of_t1Space_firstCountableTopology (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X]
    [FirstCountableTopology X] [T1Space X] : HasGδSingletons X where
  isGδ_singleton := IsGδ.singleton

findings.description: In FormalConjectures/Paper/CardinalityLindelof.lean:40–41, the existential quantifies over arbitrary topological spaces and requires only HasGδSingletons X, LindelofSpace X, and 𝔠 < #X. The source restricts its spaces to Tychonoff spaces. HasGδSingletons correctly means only that every singleton is Gδ; it does not include the missing separation condition. It implies T1Space, but even its conjunction with LindelofSpace does not imply Hausdorffness: the countable cofinite space has both properties and is not T2, as verified in Lean. Thus the use site omits an intended restriction on its witnesses.
findings.source_evidence: A. V. Arhangel’skii, Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology (2013), p. 38, explicitly states: “A ‘space’ below is a Tychonoff topological space.” On the same page, Problem 1 asks whether a Lindelöf space whose points are Gδ must have cardinality at most 2^ω, and the following paragraph requests a large counterexample in ZFC. https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf
findings.suggested_fix: Add T35Space X to the problem's existential conjunction: `∃ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T35Space X ∧ HasGδSingletons X ∧ LindelofSpace X ∧ 𝔠 < #X`. Document the source's standing Tychonoff convention. Keep the reusable HasGδSingletons definition unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Through Mathlib's IsGδ, each singleton is represented using a countable set of open sets, rather than an explicitly ℕ-indexed sequence of open neighborhoods.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An ℕ-indexed family has countable range and the same intersection. Conversely, enumerate a nonempty countable family, repeating sets when necessary; represent an empty family by the constant sequence of whole-space sets. Equality of the intersection with {x} ensures every member contains x. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, proved `HasGδSingletons X ↔ ∀ x : X, ∃ U : ℕ → Set X, (∀ n, IsOpen (U n)) ∧ (⋂ n, U n) = {x}` without extra assumptions.

review.notes: No defect found in the reviewed library's class, projection, or first-countable T₁ instance. The sole finding concerns its only problem-file use site. Lean checks covered empty and singleton types, discrete finite spaces, ℝ, indiscrete Bool, countable T₁ spaces, and the cofinite naturals. Also proved the finite-type equivalence with discreteness; finite intersection enumeration on the four two-point topologies returned [false, false, false, true]. The cofinite example establishes failure of the separation implication, not a witness to the large-cardinality requirement. The source explicitly requests a counterexample in its remarks, so the existential direction is not a separate defect; its corrected-domain equivalence to negating the universal bound was proved in /workspace/review/use-site.lean. All experiments are under /workspace/review/; no checkout files were edited.
